headline: Council removed floor area ratio limits downtown, approved $100,000 in block grant funds for a warming shelter, and ended remote public comment.
summary: The council also approved a $12,931,640 contract for airport security checkpoint expansion and a $273,902 plow truck purchase. It approved new planning fees and an ethics finding with required training for Councilor Wayne Mallar. Many residents also spoke about homelessness and the warming shelter.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including a $12,931,640 airport security contract and a $273,902 plow truck purchase.
Referred a $222,040 rental car facility appropriation and up to $65,000 for a transit director to committee and first reading.
Approved ordinance 26-293, removing floor area ratio from the Downtown Development District, 8-0.
Approved accepting and appropriating $823,851 for the Nourish Maine nutrition education program.
Approved accepting and appropriating up to $6,000 from Johns Hopkins University for a PrEP access grant.
Approved the special amusement permit for Benjamin's Restaurant and Pub, 123 Franklin Street, with no objections.
Approved the special amusement permit for Penobscot Theatre Company, 131 Main Street.
Approved ending public comment by remote means under the Remote Participation Policy, 6-2.
Approved new planning fees for abutter mailing notices and stormwater permits.
Approved amending the order for up to $100,000 in block grant funds for warming shelter and day spaces, 7-0.
Approved passing the block grant order for warming shelter and day spaces as amended, 7-0.
Approved finding that Councilor Wayne Mallar violated two ethics code provisions and must complete training, 5-2.
discussion: Warming shelter funding: Speakers urged funding for overnight warming shelters and daytime spaces during cold months, saying people could die without them. Others called the money a temporary fix and asked for housing solutions.
Remote public comment: Some speakers opposed ending remote comment, saying it helps people who cannot attend in person. Some members said disruptive remote comments had slowed meetings.
Ethics order for Councilor Mallar: Speakers disagreed over whether the ethics process had been applied evenly. Some asked that all councilors take the training.
Homelessness causes: Many speakers discussed causes of homelessness, including addiction, housing costs, low wages, and disability.
